entities.name: Eustache Deschamps
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Eustache Deschamps (c. 1346 – 1406), known by the byname Morel, was a pivotal French poet and diplomat whose extensive body of work offers an unparalleled chronicle of late 14th-century France, a period marked by the Hundred Years' War and the Western Schism. As a master of the ballade, virelai, and rondeau, Deschamps not only refined these poetic forms but also employed them as a vehicle for social commentary, political satire, and moral instruction, making him a crucial voice in the transition from late medieval courtly poetry to more personal and observational verse. His close association with the Valois court, particularly King Charles V and King Charles VI, provided him with unique insight into the political and cultural currents shaping Western Europe during a tumultuous era.

Born in Vertus, Champagne, Deschamps received a legal education, likely at Orléans, which prepared him for a career in royal service. He served as a royal bailiff and diplomat, undertaking missions across France and even into Bohemia, experiences that profoundly informed his poetry. His prodigious output includes over 1,175 ballades, numerous rondeaux, virelais, lays, and a long didactic poem, "Art de dictier" (1392), which stands as the first French treatise on poetics. In this work, he distinguished between natural music (sung) and artificial music (written verse), advocating for the latter's independent artistic merit. His verses frequently lamented the decay of chivalry, the corruption of the clergy, and the suffering of the common people amidst perpetual warfare and political instability.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Eustache Deschamps was a foundational figure in French poetics, whose "Art de dictier" established critical distinctions for verse and whose vast poetic corpus offers an invaluable, detailed historical record of late 14th-century France. His works profoundly influenced subsequent generations of French poets and provide unique insights into the social and political landscape of the Hundred Years' War era.
